nodes.name: CFC Cleaning
nodes.procedure: A piece of carbon fiber cloth 5 cm × 5 cm, CFC) was subsequently cleaned with ethanol, Millipore water and ethanol under ultrasonic, and dried in an oven before use.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of amide-functionalized CFC (A-CFC). The A-CFC was synthesized through a simple carboxylation-amidation strategy. In a typical procedure, a piece of carbon fiber cloth 5 cm × 5 cm , CFC) was subsequently cleaned with ethanol, Millipore water and ethanol under ultrasonic, and dried in an oven before use.

nodes.name: Carboxylation
nodes.procedure: The freshly cleaned CFC was then added into a stainless steel autoclave (50 mL) containing HNO3 (40 mL), and was hold at 120 °C for 20 h. The resulted c-CFC was then washed thoroughly with Millipore water.
nodes.source_text: The freshly cleaned CFC was then added into a stainless steel autoclave (50 mL) containing HNO3 (40 mL), and was hold at 120 °C for 20 h. The resulted c-CFC was then washed thoroughly with Millipore water.

nodes.name: Amidation
nodes.procedure: The freshly-prepared c-CFC was immediately [added] into another Autoclave (50 mL) containing 40 mL ammonium hydroxide solution (28% NH3 in H2O). After 20 min standing, the sealed Autoclave was placed at 150 °C for 10 h, then was naturally cooled to room temperature and washed thoroughly with Millipore water, followed by being dried in a vacuum oven for 2 h. The A-CFC was obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: A-CFC possesses a rougher, bumpy surface with deepened grooves indicating formation of more defective sites after amidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be seen from the SEM images that pure carboxylated CFC (c-CFC, Fig. 3c, d) has a smooth surface with shallow grooves, while the A-CFC possesses a rougher, bumpy surface with deepened grooves (Fig. 3f, g)

nodes.characterization_summary: Both c-CFC and A-CFC exhibit peaks at 1365.5 (D), 1594.3 (G), 2727.3 (2D) cm⁻¹; A-CFC ID/IG=0.97 > c-CFC 0.88 confirming higher defect density.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Raman spectra, both c-CFC and A-CFC exhibit three prominent peaks at 1365.5 (D peak), 1594.3 (G peak) and 2727.3 (2D peak), respectively (Supplementary Fig. 2). The larger intensity ratio of D-peaks and G-peaks (ID/IG) for A-CFC (0.97) than c-CFC (0.88) confirms the higher defect density of the A-CFC

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine c-CFC is hydrophobic with CA of 125.1±1.5° while A-CFC becomes complete wetting with CA of 0°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: pristine c-CFC is hydrophobic with a contact angle (CA) of 125.1±1.5° (Fig. 3e); after amidation, the obtained A-CFC becomes complete wetting with a CA of 0°

nodes.characterization_summary: A-CFC shows defect-rich edges with curved streaks spacing of 3.39 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM images (Fig. 4a, b) further corroborated the defect-rich edges of A-CFC and showed that the A-CFC had curved streaks with the spacing distance of 3.39 Å

nodes.characterization_summary: N elements uniformly distributed throughout the nanofibers of A-CFC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning TEM image and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mapping analysis (Fig. 4c) revealed the N elements uniformly distributed throughout the nanofibers

nodes.characterization_summary: A-CFC survey shows C, N, O elements (c-CFC: C, O only); N 1s: 399.5 eV (neutral amine N), 401.7 eV (ammonium ions); C 1s: 284.4 (C-C,H), 285.2 (C-N), 286.9 (O=C), 288.8 (O=C-N), 290.9 eV (π-π*) confirming amide groups.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS survey of A-CFC shows the presence of C, N, and O elements (Fig. 4d), while the XPS survey of c-CFC has only C and O elements. ... high-resolution N 1s spectrum showed two peaks at 399.5 and 401.7 eV corresponding to neutral amine nitrogen and ammonium ions ... C1s peak can be fitted into five peaks at 284.4, 285.2, 286.9, 288.8, and 290.9 eV, respectively, corresponding to aliphatic carbon chains (C–C,H), amine groups (C–N), carbonyl (O=C), carboxyl carbon (O=C-N), and the π-π* transitions in amides
